t: LeetCode 1616 — Split Two Strings to Make Palindrome
o: We pick one cut index applied to both strings and test the two cross-combinations a_prefix + b_suffix and b_prefix + a_suffix for palindromicity; empty prefix or suffix is allowed. Example 3 succeeds at index 3: "ula" + "alu" = "ulaalu". Trying all n+1 cuts and checking each candidate in O(n) gives an O(n²) baseline — roughly 10^10 character operations at n = 10^5, too slow. The structural observation that unlocks a linear solution: in any successful concatenation, outer mirrored pairs are supplied by different strings, while whatever remains in the middle must form a palindrome living entirely inside one of the two original strings.
k: Only two candidate strings exist per cut (a-prefix + b-suffix and its swap), and what matters is how far outer pairs match — not the cut index itself.
Greedy two pointers consume every position where a[i] == b[n-1-i]; the leftover central window must be a palindrome within a or within b alone.
Running check(a, b) || check(b, a) covers both possible cross combinations.

a.i: Enumerate all n+1 split indices, materialize both concatenations, and palindrome-test each with the classic two-pointer scan. Simple and obviously correct; only viable for small inputs because building each candidate string costs O(n).
s: For each cut i from 0 to n: form a[:i] + b[i:] and b[:i] + a[i:].
Test each formed string for being a palindrome.
Return true on the first success.
Return false after all cuts fail.
a.t: O(n²) — n+1 cuts, each producing and scanning an O(n) string; too slow for the largest inputs.

a.i: Consider x = a_prefix + b_suffix for some unknown cut. Position j and its mirror n-1-j either both fall in the prefix (both characters from a), both in the suffix (both from b), or straddle the cut (a[j] paired with b[n-1-j]). The straddling pairs are exactly what the greedy loop validates by advancing while a[l] == b[r]. Once it halts, every remaining mirrored pair lies wholly inside one original string, so the residual window [l, r] must be a palindrome within a or within b — test both. Repeating the procedure with swapped arguments covers b_prefix + a_suffix.
s: Define check(x, y): advance l and r inward while l < r and x[l] == y[r].
On stop, return isPal(x, l, r) OR isPal(y, l, r).
Answer is check(a, b) || check(b, a).
a.t: O(n) — each pointer crosses the string only a constant number of times across both check calls.
a.sp: O(1) — just indices; strings are never copied.

w:
## Wrap-up

Sketch the brute force for a minute, then derive the greedy — interviewers reward the observation about straddling pairs. **Why the leftover window suffices:** greedy matching proves all straddling pairs agree; any working split's non-straddle pairs lie entirely inside the prefix part (from a) or suffix part (from b), so a palindromic remainder must exist wholly in one string, and overshooting the greedy can only shrink that window.

**Pitfalls:** forgetting the swapped call check(b, a); testing prefixes instead of the exact residual window [l, r]; rejecting legal cuts where a side is empty (cut 0 and cut n are valid). **Edge cases:** n = 1 is always true; if a or b is already a palindrome the answer is immediately true. **Follow-ups:** return a witness cutting index, or count how many cuts work.
